description: Timestamp boundary test vectors for (canonical-content §8) — regression fixture for accept/reject decisions around clock skew and the outbound-MTA expiry window. Inbound verification has no max-age expiry: a signature stays verifiable.
notes: reference_now is a fixed anchor; real implementations compare against current system time. Tests MUST inject reference_now as the simulated 'now' when evaluating these vectors.
Each vector's offset_seconds is relative to reference_now (positive = future, negative = past).
expected_decision encodes the outcome: 'accept' (proceed to crypto verify) or 'reject' with a reason tag matching spec §8 conditions.
Context distinguishes inbound verification (every component, no max-age) from the outbound MTA (24-hour window).
Inbound verification has no max-age expiry. An earlier 7-day window no longer exists, which is why the two vectors that accept old mail carry a 'b' suffix (ts-003b, ts-004b).

vectors.description: 29 seconds into the future — within +30s clock-skew tolerance.
31 seconds into the future — exceeds +30s clock-skew tolerance.
8 days old — accepted: there is no inbound max-age.
1 year old — accepted. Integrity relies on the content hash and on revocation, not on age.
23 hours 59 minutes old — just inside the 24-hour outbound MTA window.
24 hours 1 minute old — just past the 24-hour outbound MTA window (inbound would still accept it).
vectors.spec_condition: now - timestamp > 24 hours AND context = outbound
